spans.title: The Writing on the Wall
spans.blurb: A king throws a lavish feast and drinks from stolen temple gold. Then the fingers of a human hand appear and write on the palace wall.

spans.title: David and Goliath
spans.blurb: A giant soldier taunts a terrified army for forty days, until a shepherd boy delivering bread to his brothers asks why nobody has answered him.

spans.title: We're All Mad Here
spans.blurb: Lost at a crossroads, a girl asks a grinning cat for directions and receives logic, a diagnosis of madness, and an invitation to croquet.

spans.title: A Mad Tea Party
spans.blurb: A girl sits down uninvited at an endless tea table, where the riddles have no answers, the watch runs on butter, and it is always six o'clock.

spans.title: There's Glory for You
spans.blurb: Humpty Dumpty quizzes a polite girl on birthdays and arithmetic, then announces that a word means exactly what he chooses it to mean.

spans.title: Tweedledum and Tweedledee
spans.blurb: Two round brothers agree to battle over a spoiled new rattle, armoured in bolsters and coal scuttles, while something dark flies toward the wood.

spans.title: A Dog for a Nurse
spans.blurb: A tidy London family cannot afford a proper nurse, so they engage a Newfoundland dog named Nana, who takes childcare very seriously indeed.

spans.title: The Boy Who Lost His Shadow
spans.blurb: A crying boy breaks into a nursery hunting for his lost shadow, and the girl who wakes knows exactly what to do about it.

spans.title: Evil, Be Thou My Good
spans.blurb: A ruined spirit, utterly alone, asks whether any way back remains, and talks himself out of every answer but one.

spans.title: The Thief and the Innkeeper
spans.blurb: A guest who cannot pay his bill yawns, howls like a wolf, and politely asks the innkeeper to hold his clothes.

spans.title: The Ships in the Bay
spans.blurb: From a high bank above the Chesapeake, an enslaved boy watches white sails glide out to freedom and pours his whole heart after them.

spans.title: The Battle with Covey
spans.blurb: Carrying a root said to protect him from any whipping, an enslaved young man decides one Monday morning that he will fight back.

spans.title: No Place for Repentance
spans.blurb: Alone with himself, a fallen spirit weighs pardon against pride, counts what surrender would cost him, and makes his choice.

spans.title: The Gates of Hell
spans.blurb: A fleeing rebel spirit reaches ninefold gates of brass, iron, and rock, and finds two monstrous shapes guarding them, one wearing the likeness of a crown.
spans.spoilerNote: Hints that the shapes guarding the gate are Satan's own kin, a disclosure the poem stages as a revelation just after this scene.
spans.brokenNote: The passage opens and closes mid-sentence, cutting off Satan's reply before the standoff resolves.

spans.title: No Trickery
spans.blurb: After dinner, an inventor asks his sceptical guests to examine a beautifully made little machine, then invites one of them to press the lever.

spans.title: The White Sphinx
spans.blurb: A reckless traveller hurls himself into futurity, then risks everything to stop. He lands in hail and blossoms under the gaze of a marble sphinx.

spans.title: The Thing in the Pit
spans.blurb: A crowd gathers at a pit expecting a man to climb out of the fallen cylinder. What emerges instead glistens like wet leather.
spans.spoilerNote: Shows what the invaders actually look like, a horror the book builds up to across its opening chapters.

spans.title: The Third Falling Star
spans.blurb: Driving home near midnight under a gathering storm, a man sees a green thread of fire fall into a field, and then something enormous begins to walk.
spans.spoilerNote: Reveals the invaders' giant walking machines, whose first appearance the book stages as a shock.
